summary: In this excerpt from Book 14, the narrator rides home after a gathering with Ian, Geoff, and Zeke, a brilliant, unconventional young man who sleeps in the back seat of Ian's rental car. Zeke apologizes for teasing the narrator's name and admits he had pictured a different person named Shad, then laughs at the name Zenobia. Ian explains Zeke's background: he knew him since age twelve, Zeke dropped out of one of Ian's classes, avoids rules and money, and travels freely while earning freelance income. The passage closes with Ian beginning to describe how being accepted to MIT at fourteen can affect social skills.
one_line: A snowy night ride home from a party in Book 14, where Ian describes the unconventional, brilliant friend Zeke.
key_facts: Zeke apologized to the narrator for making fun of the narrator's name, and the narrator said they were used to it.
Zeke said he was still trying to match the narrator up with Shad and had a different picture in his head, 'Not a girl.'
Zeke was called 'Zeke the Freak' during his first two minutes at preschool.
Zeke said that the narrator was named Zenobia, which set him howling with laughter again.
Jason and Tyler stayed behind to take apart the traveling Faraday cage and erase all signs of the party's presence.
Outside, the freezing rain had turned into snow, and Ian said the narrator could not ride a bike in such weather.
The narrator took the front wheel off their bike and stowed it and the bike in Ian's trunk.
Zeke did not have a car, and he stretched out across the back seat of Ian's rental car and began to snore.
Zeke hitched a ride up from Chicago with a truck driver and had no place to stay.
Ian has known Zeke since Zeke was twelve years old.
Zeke took a class from Ian when he was younger than the narrator, but dropped out before the semester ended.
Ian describes Zeke as brilliant but uninterested in following rules or filling out forms, and as someone who thinks money is stupid.
Zeke learns whatever he finds interesting and picks up freelance work to make a living, traveling constantly and having friends everywhere.
Ian says Zeke can be kind of a jerk sometimes, and the narrator replies, 'I noticed.'
Ian says being accepted to MIT at fourteen can mess up one's grasp of social skills.
